response.content: {"visual":{"fullPrompt":"Handheld macro-leaning close-up, modern social-first beauty campaign photography with tactile editorial energy, 16:9. SCARLETT VEGA stands at a hole-in-the-wall dumpling shop's takeout window wearing a fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed to the elbows, a slouchy dark denim-canvas jacket hanging off one shoulder, dark slim jeans, small gold hoop earrings and a thin silver ring on her right index finger, a heavy natural-canvas tote strap cutting across her chest. She is caught mid-beat: a bitten dumpling half pinched in her fingers just lowered from her mouth, jaw barely closed mid-chew, her other hand pressing a thin white napkin to the corner of her lips and beginning to peel it away, the napkin's edge crisp and unmarked, her eyebrow lifting a fraction as her eyes cut directly into the lens with deadpan amusement. In front of her a scratched stainless steel window ledge holds a soggy-edged paper tray of dumplings with steam curling up in visible ropes through the light, a squeeze bottle of glossy bright red chili oil, and a leaning stack of thin napkins at the counter's edge. Behind the ledge the takeout window glows warm yellow fluorescent from inside, a plastic-sleeved handwritten menu taped to the glass gone soft in the haze, a red awning cropping the top of frame, a half-raised roll-down security gate at the edge. Deep blue-black narrow side street behind her with old brick, a fire escape ladder and distant traffic reduced to soft round bokeh. The warm fluorescent spill from the window is the key, wrapping her cheek and catching wet highlights on the chili oil and the steel, while cool ambient street light fills the shadow side for a clean crisp contrast; true-to-life color, whites kept bright, lifted airy shadows, one warm coral accent popping against the neutral steel and black.
